concerns.text: FR-005 requires determining 'statistical significance (p < 0.05)' for RMSE/MAE/R² metrics. However, the spec does not define the statistical test to be used (e.g., paired t-test, Wilcoxon signed-rank) to generate this p-value when comparing the model against the null baseline. Without specifying the test, the requirement is ambiguous and potentially unimplementable as written.

FR-007 mandates reporting 'false-positive and false-negative rates' for a regression task (biomass prediction). Regression models output continuous values, not binary classifications, so standard FP/FN rates are undefined unless a specific decision threshold (e.g., 'biomass > X tons') is defined. The requirement lacks the definition of this threshold or the conversion logic from continuous prediction to binary class.

The Assumptions section states: 'The sensitivity analysis will sweep the decision threshold over the absolute difference set {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}'. This contradicts the regression nature of the problem (biomass prediction) where 'decision thresholds' for FP/FN rates (as mentioned in FR-007) are not applicable without a defined classification boundary. The assumption reinforces the ambiguity in FR-007 regarding the nature of the 'threshold' being swept.
